plan: In a single-round sealed bid ascending auction with a private value of $31, my optimal strategy is to bid strategically. Since values are independently drawn, I want to balance winning probability with profit margin. A bid close to my true value but slightly below could maximize expected profit. I'll aim to bid around $25-$28 - low enough to preserve potential profit, but high enough to have a reasonable chance of winning against potential competitor bids.

In a single-round sealed bid auction with a private value of $6, my goal is to maximize potential profit. Since the auction uses an ascending clock mechanism, I want to bid strategically. A bid slightly above my value ($6) could help me win if others bid conservatively, but bidding too high risks losing money. Given the uncertainty and single-round nature, I'll bid around $6.50 to create a modest buffer while staying close to my true value.

With a private value of $0, my optimal strategy is to bid $0. Since I have no inherent value in the item, any positive bid would only risk losing money. In a sealed bid auction, bidding my true value (zero) minimizes potential losses. My goal is to avoid paying more than the item is worth to me. Even if other bidders bid higher, I will not incur any cost or loss by bidding $0.
